chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with two witnesses, then took her back, and did not have intercourse with her after the revocation until she purified from her menses, then he divorced her again while she was pure, with two witnesses. Does the second divorce take effect, given that he took her back and did not have intercourse with her? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.رَاجَعَهَا: he took her back (revoked the divorce)

ai.seo_question: Does a husband need to have sexual intercourse with his wife after revoking the divorce for the second divorce to be valid?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the validity of the second divorce (talqah thaniyah) does not hinge on sexual intercourse following the initial revocation (raj'a), but rather on the wife observing a full menstrual cycle (tuhr) after the revocation. This ruling, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the ritual purity period as the definitive marker for the completion of the waiting period (iddah) in cases of revocable divorce, distinguishing it from consummation requirements in other contexts.
